## ✨ Highlights

HAProxy maintenance releases on every branch, and a security fix for the
Controller's updater.

- 🔀 **HAProxy 3.4.9, 3.2.28 and 3.0.32**: 165, 125 and 112 bug fixes.
  None of the vulnerabilities they fix applies to Janus's build: the
  only one rated high is in HTTP/3, which Janus's HAProxy doesn't build.
- 🔒 **Docker Compose v5.8.1** in the Controller's updater: a crash on
  crafted compressed data, rated high.
- 🐧 **kexec reboots**: the kernel now carries the upstream EFI
  maintainer's fix in place of ours.

## 🔒 Security

- **Docker Compose (Controller updater) v5.8.0 → v5.8.1** (the Controller):
  - 🟠 high [CVE-2026-116591](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6865) - Panic on two-block frames in github.com/klauspost/compress

What it means:

- **Only the Controller's updater is concerned**
  (`janus-controller-updater`, the container that runs `docker compose`
  to update the Controller). Crafted compressed data could make
  `docker-compose` panic, which stops it. Nodes and the Controller's own
  process don't run Compose.
- **What to do**: update the Controller, then run `docker compose up
  -d` once in its directory. The updater keeps running the image it was
  started with until the next `docker compose up -d` gives it the new
  one ([What an update does](https://janus.sw-servers.net/docs/dashboard/README.md#what-an-update-does)).
- **The HAProxy releases fix no vulnerability that applies to Janus's
  build**. The one rated high (`BUG/MAJOR: h3: prevent demux full
  BUG_ON() crash with incomplete DATA`, all three branches) is in
  HTTP/3, and Janus's HAProxy is built without QUIC. The others change
  files that aren't built (Lua, QUIC...). The Controller's update badge
  (🔒) doesn't show on nodes for this release.

## 🔀 HAProxy

- **HAProxy 3.4.8 → 3.4.9** (the default branch), **3.2.27 → 3.2.28**
  and **3.0.31 → 3.0.32** (nodes pinned to them)
  ([#723](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/723)). The fixes that
  matter most on a Janus node:
  - **Clusters**: `peers` now bound the size of the stick-table
    messages they send and receive and trim over-long string keys;
    string keys are sharded on the key as stored; a soft stop keeps
    each `peers` section's state apart.
  - **Runtime API**: `add ssl crt-list` - what the node uses to bind an
    uploaded certificate - keeps the certificate's settings, also when
    it fails; `set table` without a key no longer clears the whole
    table.
  - **HTTP/2**: connection timeouts refreshed when a connection is
    parked idle or still has data to send, buffer allocations no
    longer stalled, a `2xx` other than `101` refused in answer to an
    extended `CONNECT`.
  - **kTLS** (3.4): a short read is no longer taken for the end of the
    data.
  - **DNS resolution** (`resolvers`): records HAProxy ignores are
    skipped properly, expired TCP queries free their slot.

## 🐧 Kernel

- **kexec reboots** (a node's reboot or update with `kexec` as its
  reboot mode): v2026.10.12 fixed a kernel started by kexec clearing 16
  bytes of memory at an address left over from the boot before - under
  some firmware, inside its own code. The EFI maintainer declined our
  fix and wrote another: on x86, a kernel started by kexec now ignores
  the tables the EFI stub left for the first kernel. Janus builds both
  kernel tracks with his commit until a 7.3.y / 6.18.y release carries
  it ([#716](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/716),
  [#374](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/issues/374)). Nothing changes
  for a node: kexec reboots work as before, firmware reboots were never
  concerned.

## ⚠️ Upgrade notes

- **HAProxy now refuses a few invalid settings it used to accept**, in
  every branch: a negative `capture` length, a negative stick counter
  number in `sc-*` actions, a `gpc`/`gpt` index out of range, `resolve_retries`,
  `timeout resolve` or `timeout retry` at 0 in a `resolvers`
  section, servers sharing one SRV record through different
  `resolvers`, a value that isn't a number in a `tune.h2.*` keyword.
  None of them ever worked. A node whose configuration has one can't
  start HAProxy on the new release, so look for them **before**
  updating: the node's own check runs the HAProxy it has, which still
  accepts them. With `-wait-for-health`, on by default on the
  Controller's Update page, a node that can't start HAProxy goes back
  to its previous slot by itself, about a minute after its reboot.

## 🧪 Tests and tooling

- **OpenTofu 1.13.10** (was 1.13.9) drives the Terraform provider's
  tests ([#723](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/723)).
- `qemu-kexec-test` checks that both kexec'd kernels ignore the stale
  INITRD table and that the firmware boots still list it
  ([#716](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/716)).
- v2026.11.24's lab campaign
  ([#715](https://github.com/swenske/Janus/pull/715)).
